text: Notes on Partial Fractions Here are some notes on partial fractions. Everything here is discussed in the text, with the exception of item (d) below. Overview. The method of partial fractions is used to ﬁnd antiderivatives of rational functions, that is, functions of the form p(x) q(x) where p and q are polynomials. The fraction p(x) q(x) is a proper fraction if deg(p) < deg(q). The method of partial fractions applies to proper fractions only. Outline. Here is an outline of the method. (a) First use long division to obtain a proper fraction. The remaining steps assume that deg(p) <deg(q)!! (b) Factor the denominator q(x) completely into a product of linear and irreducible quadratic factors. (A quadradic is irreducible if it has no real roots.) (c) For each factor of the form (ax + b)n, use fractions of the form, A1 ax + b + A2 (ax + b)2 + · · · + An (ax + b)n . (1) Remark: Frequently, n = 1, in which case formula (1) is just A ax + b . (d) For each irreducible factor of the form (ax2 + bx + c)m, use fractions of the form, A1x + B1 ax2 + bx + c + A2x + B2 (ax2 + bx + c)2 + · · · + Amx + Bm (ax2 + bx + c)m . (2) Remark: Often, m = 1, in which case formula (2) is just Ax + B ax2 + bx + c . (e) Set p(x) q(x) equal to the sum of all the fractions obtained in the previous two steps. (f) Use algebra to ﬁnd all the coeﬃcients. B) Optional Exercises: Find the antiderivatives using the method of partial fractions. (You may also need to use other techniques too.) 1) ∫ dx x2 + x 2) ∫ x dx x2 − x − 6 3) ∫ dt t3 − 1 4) ∫ 2s3 − s2 − 4s + 5 s2 + 1 ds
